title: KPI Drift Detector, Gating & Escalation Canvas
content:
Purpose:
This canvas defines an operationally-actionable KPI drift detector for staged rollouts. It codifies the metrics to monitor, statistical gating rules, automated severity levels, and the escalation + rollback playbook owners. Goal: reduce noisy manual checks and ensure consistent, repeatable go/no-go decisions during pilot -> canary -> scale phases.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to any product-ops managed rollout (hosted API feature flags, dedicated capacity changes, model version swaps).
- Focused on user-facing signal classes: latency, error-rate, token-cost-per-request, correctness/regression (eval-based), and adoption (relative traffic share).
- Assumes telemetry is available via Console telemetry + Prometheus + evaluation harness and that alerts can trigger runbook steps (PagerDuty / Slack).
- This is a living canvas: thresholds are defaults and must be tuned per feature and customer cohort.

Primary signals (one-line definitions):
- p95-latency-ms: 95th percentile end-to-end response latency in ms (API ingress -> model response complete).
- request-error-rate: 5xx + model-failed responses as a fraction of total successful attempts (windowed).
- token-cost-per-request: billable token units averaged per request (includes prompt + completion tokens).
- semantic-regression-score: automated eval pass-rate on golden prompt set (weighted).
- real-user-dropoff: fraction of sessions that drop after receiving an LLM response (proxy for quality).

Measurement windows and aggregation:
- Baseline window: 7 days pre-rollout or last steady-state week for the route/model combo.
- Comparison window: rolling 5-minute windows for alerting, 1-hour windows for gating decisions, 24-hour windows for post-launch review.
- Minimum sample sizes: n>=200 requests per 1-hour window for gating; n>=1000 for robust statistical checks across large cohorts.
- Aggregation: route-level, model-variant-level, and customer-tier slices (enterprise vs self-serve).

Statistical gating logic (default):
- For rate and latency metrics: use non-parametric bootstrap CI on the metric difference vs baseline. Gate fires when lower bound of 95% CI for the delta exceeds the configurable threshold.
- For error-rate: use two-proportion z-test with continuity correction; require p<0.01 AND absolute delta > 0.5 percentage points to trigger severity 2.
- For semantic-regression-score: require a drop of >=2.5 percentage points OR 1.5 stdev below baseline across golden set.
- For low-sample scenarios: fall back to heuristic thresholds and label as "uncertain" (do not auto-rollback; require human review).

Default thresholds (tunable by feature):
- p95-latency-ms: +40% relative increase OR +150ms absolute increase -> Severity 2; +80% OR +300ms -> Severity 1 (critical).
- request-error-rate: +0.5pp -> Sev 2; +1.5pp -> Sev 1.
- token-cost-per-request: +25% -> cost-watch (no immediate gating) ; +50% -> Sev 3 (product review).
- semantic-regression-score: -2.5pp -> Sev 2; -5pp -> Sev 1.
- real-user-dropoff: +3pp -> Sev 2; +7pp -> Sev 1.

Severity mapping and automated actions:
- Sev 3 (informational): post to rollout-channel, owner notified; continue monitoring.
- Sev 2 (action recommended - canary hold): pause automatic traffic increase, pin rollout percentage, trigger deep-dive runbook (owner analyst + SRE).
- Sev 1 (critical - auto-fallback): automatically shift traffic to previous stable model/route or reduce to safe lowest tier; fire PagerDuty; initiate rollback runbook.

Escalation matrix (owner roles):
- Primary Owner: feature product manager (PM) -> responsible for business decision, communicates customer impact.
- Metric Steward: product-ops analyst -> owns dashboards, root-cause slice prep, forensic queries.
- Infra/SRE: owns deployment and routing fallbacks, executes traffic shifts and capacity patches.
- ML Owner: model owner/researcher -> runs offline evals and inspects model-specific regressions.
- Oncall: PagerDuty engineer (primary) -> executes automated playbook steps if auto-actions incomplete.

Rolled actions checklist (playbook snippets):
1) Sev 3: collect top-10 affected routes, post summary with CI and heatmap; owner acknowledges within 60 minutes.
2) Sev 2 (canary hold): keep traffic pinned; run focused A/B slices comparing variant vs baseline on last 2 hours; run smoke tests (100 golden prompts); if regression reproducible -> escalate to Sev 1 OR schedule hotfix.
3) Sev 1 (auto-fallback): traffic shift (precomputed route alias) -> 100% -> stable; invalidate recent model cache if applicable; publish postmortem stub and assign RCA owner.

Decision timeline and guardrails:
- Time-to-decision targets: Sev2 owner ack in 30m, decision to hold or roll-forward in 90m. Sev1 auto-action within 5m of trigger.
- Human override window: even after auto-fallback, PM may request roll-forward if mitigation validated; requires documented rationale in rollout channel.
- Canary sizing: initial canary <= 5% traffic and must pass 24h without Sev2/Sev1 signals before scheduled ramp.

Runbook templates to attach to alerts (short form):
- "Investigate-Latency-Spike": top-three queries by token-length, model-variant latency distribution, infra host CPU/GPU utilization.
- "Investigate-Semantic-Drift": run eval harness on last-1000 user prompts, compare perplexity/QA-accuracy against baseline, inspect tokenization diffs.
- "Rollback-Execution": route alias switch, cache invalidation, notify infra + SRE + PM, adjust monitoring flags.

Metrics dashboard layout (board recipe):
- Row 1: immediate health (p50/p95/p99 latency) + request-error-rate + throughput per route.
- Row 2: drift detector deltas (metric vs baseline with CI), sample counts, and uncertainty flag.
- Row 3: cost telemetry (tokens per request, cost per 10k requests), projected monthly delta.
- Row 4: golden-set semantic regression panel (pass rate, per-prompt failures).

Ownership and naming conventions:
- Alert names: prod.kpi.drift.<route>.<metric>.<severity> (e.g., prod.kpi.drift.chat-complete.p95.sev2).
- Runbook links must be attached to the alert; page must include the most recent forensic query SQL/PromQL.
- Owner oncall rotation documented in product-ops/team-runbook.

Postmortem and learning loop:
- Any Sev1 incident triggers a 72-hour RCA cadence: initial stub (24h), interim notes (48h), final RCA (72h) with action owners and deadlines.
- Maintain a short "lessons learned" registry with tuning suggestions for thresholds per feature category (e.g., low-latency streaming vs batch embedding routes).

Tuning and rollout checklist for owners (preflight):
- Confirm baseline computed on comparable traffic (same user cohorts) and not across an unrelated route.
- Generate golden prompt suite (min 200 prompts) representative of critical behaviors.
- Confirm telemetry alignment (same timezones, ingestion pipeline and metric tags).
- Predefine per-feature thresholds in feature flag config (not hard-coded inside alerting rules).
- Schedule a smoke window with engineering during first 24h of canary.

Open questions / To-dos (working list):
- Explore embedding ML-based anomaly detection to supplement statistical rules for low-sample signals (owner: Ethan).
- Integrate semantic-regression evaluation into streaming pipeline for near-real-time gating (owner: Maya).
- Add automated cost-scenario simulator to show projected monthly spend changes for each rollout (owner: Priya).

Quick reference (cheat-sheet):
- Canary <=5% for 24h -> no Sev2/Sev1 -> ramp stepwise (5->25->50->100) with 1-hour observation windows.
- Sev2 = pause ramp; Sev1 = auto-fallback + PD.
- Always attach golden-set results and sample counts when posting a Sev2/Sev1 alert.

Appendix: Example alert body (template)
- Subject: [ALERT] prod.kpi.drift.chat-complete.p95.sev2
- Body: metric: p95-latency-ms; baseline: 180ms; current: 310ms; delta: +72% (95% CI lower bound +45%); samples: 3,200 (1h); immediate action: canary hold; links: dashboard, runbook, forensic query.

Document history and notes:
- Created to standardize decisioning across Dedicated and Hosted API rollouts where cost/latency tradeoffs are frequent.
- Draft status: please add per-feature tuning suggestions in the linked Confluence page.

---
Notes to self (short): prioritize integrations with Console "per-route" telemetry and ensure alert noise baseline by excluding scheduled maintenance windows.
